title: “A Few Good Men” is now playing on Broadway at Lincoln Center’s Vivia...
transcript: A lot of people may not realize that before it was a four time Oscar nominated film, A Few Good Men was actually a stage show first. And now that play, also written by Aaron Sorkin, is back on Broadway, this time starring Tom Blyth and Bradley Whitford. Now somehow I've never actually seen the movie or the play before, so this was actually my first experience with the material and I have to say I found the story pretty captivating. It is about two Marines who have been arrested for the murder of a fellow Marine. And while it initially seems like a pretty open and shut case, it eventually becomes clear that there's actually more than meets the eye. And not only are these two men likely innocent, but proving it could expose some deeper systemic issues within the Marines themselves. Our main character is the lawyer for these two men, played by Tom Blyth, with Whitford playing the commanding officer, attempting to cover it all up. There is also a massive supporting cast made up of many of Broadway's finest, including Krysta Rodriguez, Nick Blaemire, Thom Sesma and a criminally underutilized Billy Eugene Jones. If this production has one flaw, it's that it's just a bit bland. Director Michael Arden has become known for revivals that breathe new life into the material, from deaf west spring awakening to once on this island to parade. But this is more or less a straightforward production of A few Good men. He's not really taking any big swings here. And as for the play itself, while I was consistently entertained, it didn't really have any big wow moment for me. Perhaps because it's climax is one of the most famous scenes in all of cinema, and in fact, the only scene from the film that I've actually seen. And knowing more or less how it ends definitely takes the wind out of the sails a little bit. Still, there is a lot to enjoy about this play, notably Aaron Sorkin's script. It's quite a compelling underdog story as this scrappy legal team tries to take on the Marine establishment. And because of that, I'm going to give it a Broadway Ben recommendation.
